treeshapesim: Simulate Trees with Separately Controlled Imbalance and Branching Times

Source: R/treeshapesim-package.R
treeshapesim-package.Rd

Simulates rooted, binary, ultrametric trees in which topological imbalance and the distribution of branching times are set by separate parameters, and estimates those parameters from empirical trees.

Terms

Topology

The branching pattern of a tree, without branch lengths.

Imbalance

How unequally the tips are divided between the two daughter clades of the internal nodes, measured here by the Colless index normalized against its expectation under the Yule model (see tree_shape()).

beta

The parameter of Aldous' (1996) beta-splitting model of topologies: beta = 0 gives the distribution of Yule topologies, lower values more imbalanced and higher values more balanced topologies.

Internode intervals

The times \(g_k\) during which the tree has \(k\) lineages, from the root (\(k = 2\)) to the present (\(k = n\)).

c

The exponent of the dependence of the per-lineage split rate on the number of lineages \(k\), \(k^c\); c = 0 is a Yule process.

gamma

Pybus and Harvey's (2000) statistic of the internode intervals: negative when splits are concentrated near the root.

Sampling fraction

The proportion of the species of a clade that are in the tree.

Algorithms

The combination of a beta-splitting topology with intervals from a lineage-dependent pure-birth process, joined by a uniform random ranking of the internal nodes, is, as far as we know, a new algorithm; this is its first implementation. The estimators of beta (maximum likelihood under beta-splitting) and of c (the density-dependent exponential model) were implemented in the R packages apTreeshape and laser, both archived on CRAN; fit_shape() reimplements them and adds a correction of c for incomplete sampling, which is new.

Life cycle

The package is in active development and its interface is experimental (version 0.x): function names and arguments may still change, with changes listed in NEWS.md. The core simulators (sim_tree_shape(), rtopology_beta(), intervals_lineage_rate(), assign_ages()) are expected to be stable; planned work, including a sampler with extinction and a CRAN release, is listed in ROADMAP.md in the source repository.

References

Aldous, D. (1996). Probability distributions on cladograms. In D. Aldous & R. Pemantle (Eds.), Random discrete structures (pp. 1–18). Springer. doi:10.1007/978-1-4612-0719-1_1

Pybus, O. G., & Harvey, P. H. (2000). Testing macro-evolutionary models using incomplete molecular phylogenies. Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 267, 2267–2272. doi:10.1098/rspb.2000.1278
